pages.text: Electro Energetics carries power through $(thing)Connectors$(0) joined by wire. Pick up a wire spool, use it on one connector, then on another, to string a wire between them.$(br2)Use an $(thing)Empty Spool$(0) on a wire to take it down again.$(br2)Like real circuits, every load needs a path out and back. Run two wires, or return the current through the ground with a $(thing)Ground Rod$(0).
Fired clay bodies with a copper terminal. Double, triple and quad connectors carry several circuits on one block.

$(bold)Wire types$(0)$(br)$(li)$(thing)Copper / Electrum$(0): bare wire, cheap and conductive$(li)$(thing)Insulated$(0): rubber-wrapped copper, safe to touch, can be dyed$(li)$(thing)Heavily Insulated$(0): paper-and-oil cable in a lead sheath, for high voltage near people$(li)$(thing)ACSR Conductor$(0): aluminium around a steel core, for long overhead lines$(li)$(thing)Bus / Rail$(0): stiff conductors for substations and third rails

Wire is wound onto lathe-turned $(thing)Empty Spools$(0) by deployers on a sequenced-assembly line. Most wire comes from the rolling mill.$(br2)Overhead lines hang from $(thing)Pole Mounts$(0) on poles, insulated by porcelain $(thing)Insulators$(0) or strings of $(thing)Glass Insulator$(0) segments.

$(bold)Losses and voltage$(0)$(br)Every wire has resistance, and the energy it wastes grows with the $(italic)square$(0) of the current.$(br2)To send power far, step the voltage up with a $(thing)Transformer$(0) at the plant and down again near the machines. Same power, less current, much smaller losses.
The turns ratio sets the voltage ratio. Surround the core with Radiator Panels and cover it in Transformer Oil to raise its power rating; overloading it damages it.
